pattern.name: TDD Catches Infrastructure Bugs Early
pattern.description: Validation mission discovered 100% pattern loss BEFORE it reached production. Tests written FIRST caught the violation immediately. Zero production impact (caught in development).
pattern.insight: Test infrastructure BEFORE claiming success prevents costly production bugs
evidence: Validation mission discovered 100% VectorStore pattern loss
Tests written FIRST caught violation immediately
Zero production impact (caught in development phase)
8 test failures = immediate red flag
Fix applied before any production deployment
pattern.applicability: All infrastructure changes, especially default parameter changes
pattern.when_to_apply: ALWAYS test infrastructure changes before claiming success
expected_outcomes: Zero production bugs from infrastructure changes
Reduced debugging time (catch at development vs production)
pattern.anti_pattern: Deploy infrastructure changes without validation tests

pattern.name: Default Parameter Anti-Patterns Are Dangerous
pattern.description: Memory(store=None) defaulting to ephemeral storage caused systemic violation. Easy to violate constitution accidentally (footgun API). Fix: Safety-first defaults (persistent by default, ephemeral by choice).
pattern.insight: Defaults should enforce safety and constitutional compliance, not convenience
evidence: Memory(store=None) defaulted to InMemoryStore (ephemeral)
100% pattern loss across all agents
Silent failure (no error, no warning, code ran successfully)
Easy to violate constitution accidentally
Fixed by changing default to EnhancedMemoryStore (persistent)
pattern.applicability: All API design with default parameters
pattern.when_to_apply: When designing APIs with optional parameters that affect safety/compliance
expected_outcomes: Explicit opt-out for unsafe behavior (not opt-in for safety)
pattern.anti_pattern: Unsafe/non-compliant defaults that require explicit opt-in for safety

code_example.before:
def __init__(self, store=None):
    self._store = store or InMemoryStore()  # Ephemeral by default (BAD)
code_example.after:
def __init__(self, store=None):
    self._store = store or EnhancedMemoryStore()  # Persistent by default (GOOD)

pattern.name: Backward Compatibility Prevents Breaking Changes
pattern.description: Explicit memory parameter still works (85/85 tests PASS). Zero regressions in existing code. Migration path: change defaults, preserve overrides.
pattern.insight: Always preserve explicit parameters when changing defaults
evidence: 85/85 tests passed (existing code zero regressions)
Explicit memory=InMemoryStore() still works (backward compatible)
Only default changed (Memory() now uses EnhancedMemoryStore)
Migration path clear: change defaults, preserve overrides
Zero breaking changes to existing code
pattern.applicability: All default parameter changes, API migrations
pattern.when_to_apply: When changing defaults or migrating to new implementations
expected_outcomes: Zero breaking changes to existing code
New code gets better defaults automatically
pattern.anti_pattern: Change defaults AND remove old parameter support simultaneously

code_example.migration_strategy:
# Phase 1: Change default (backward compatible)
def __init__(self, store=None):
    self._store = store or EnhancedMemoryStore()  # New default
    # Explicit store=InMemoryStore() still works

# Phase 2 (future): Deprecation warning
if isinstance(store, InMemoryStore):
    logger.warning('InMemoryStore deprecated, use EnhancedMemoryStore')

# Phase 3 (future): Remove support
# Only after all code migrated

pattern.name: Documentation vs Reality Gaps Are Critical
pattern.description: CLAUDE.md claimed 'VectorStore integration is MANDATORY'. Reality: InMemoryStore was the actual default. Impact: Trust erosion, false confidence in learning capabilities.
pattern.insight: Documentation must match implementation, or trust collapses
evidence: CLAUDE.md: 'VectorStore integration is MANDATORY'
Reality: Memory() created InMemoryStore (ephemeral)
Documentation-reality gap caused months of silent failure
Trust erosion (documentation not trustworthy)
False confidence in learning capabilities
pattern.when_to_apply: ALWAYS validate documentation against actual implementation
pattern.anti_pattern: Update documentation without validating against implementation

validation_strategy.automated_tests: Test documentation claims (e.g., test VectorStore is default)

pattern.name: Result Pattern Enables Composable Error Handling
pattern.description: Article IV validator returns Result<bool, str> (not exceptions). Composable with other validators (no control flow via exceptions). Clear success/failure paths without try/catch.
pattern.insight: Result<T,E> pattern is superior to exception-based control flow
evidence: validate_article_iv() returns Result<bool, str>
Composable with other validators (no exception catching needed)
Clear success/failure paths (no hidden control flow)
Easier to test (no exception mocking required)
Better error context (string reason vs exception stack)
pattern.when_to_apply: When operations can fail and error handling is composable
